newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT - AT&T third quarter net declines.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - AT&T third quarter net declines.

text.p: AT&T Corp said Thursday volume growth in its consumer telephony business picked up in the third quarter over the second. It also reported third quarter net income from continuing operations of $1.359 billion, or $0.84 a share, a more than 12 pct decline compared with $0.96 a share in the year-ago quarter.
This is the full text of its announcement.

NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)--October 17, 1996--AT&T today reported third-quarter net income from continuing operations of $1.359 billion or 84 cents per share. As expected, income declined nearly 11 percent from $1.525 billion, while earnings per share declined more than 12 percent from 96 cents in the comparable period last year.

On September 24, AT&T announced that its third-quarter earnings for continuing operations appeared to be as much as 10 percent below the mean estimate of 92 cents per share of key analysts who follow the company. As reasons for the shortfall, the company cited its investments in local, on-line and wireless capabilities, customer care enhancements and its efforts to address competitive pressures in long distance.

As previously reported, AT&T is required to reformat its results reporting to reflect the spinoff of Lucent Technologies, the sale of AT&T Capital Corp., and the expected spinoff of NCR. In addition, AT&T's submarine systems and new media businesses are now included in "discontinued operations," and previously reported results have been restated to exclude these businesses from continuing operations.

Earnings for the consolidated AT&T, including income from operations to be discontinued, were $1.432 billion, or 89 cents per share, compared with $262 million or 16 cents per share in the year-ago quarter. The year-ago quarter included a pre-tax charge of $1.6 billion for the restructuring and cost-reduction effort at NCR.

With the September 30 spinoff of Lucent and the October 1 sale of AT&T Capital complete, the third-quarter results released today are the last time these companies' results will be included in AT&T's quarterly reporting.

"We have accomplished a great deal since we announced AT&T's strategic restructuring 13 months ago," said AT&T Chairman Robert E. Allen. "Most people have focused on our extremely ambitious timetable to spin off Lucent Technologies, sell AT&T Capital Corp., turn around NCR Corp. and begin the process for its spinoff. But we've also focused on restructuring and creating the new' AT&T. Much is being done to dramatically reshape our business and focus on future products and services.

"As I said a month ago, our earnings are less than we would have liked. In some parts of the business, we've done very well; in other areas, the results of our efforts showed less improvement than we had hoped. But our top priority is to create shareowner value and to do it in ways that fundamentally strengthen the new AT&T for the long haul. We are building for the future," Allen said.
Revenue from continuing operations increased more than 2 percent to $13.228 billion, compared with the restated $12.920 billion in the year-ago quarter.

For the nine months ending September 30, the company's net income from continuing operations was $4.366 billion, or $2.71 a share, on revenues of $38.946 billion. For the same period last year, net income was $4.153 billion, or $2.61 a share, on revenues of $37.778 billion.

For the quarter, communications services revenue increased $497 million or 4 percent from the same period last year. Communications services revenues include wireline services, wireless services as well as communications products and other services.

Wireline services revenue, which includes inter- and intra- LATA toll, network management, satellite, messaging and other network enabled services, increased slightly more than 2 percent for the quarter to $11.552 billion. The growth in long distance revenues came primarily from U.S. business services. Long distance calling volumes grew slightly more than 5 percent over the same period in 1995.

In response to the competitive environment and price misperceptions, the company recently announced AT&T One Rate (SM), its new and simple calling plan offering 15 cents-a- minute calls 24 hours a day, seven days a week in the U.S. While competitive pressure continues in the consumer business, volume growth shows improvement over the previous quarter, particularly in international.

Wireless services revenue, which includes cellular voice and data, messaging and air-to-ground, grew 17.7 percent to $892 million for the third quarter. Consolidated cellular service subscribers grew to 4.78 million, a 33.3 percent increase from a year ago. In addition to adding approximately 245,000 subscribers, the wireless unit also announced AT&T Digital PCS in 40 major metropolitan markets, which allows new features such as caller ID, message waiting indicators and short messaging as well as improved fraud protection.

Revenues from communications products and other services, which include consulting and outsourcing, on-line, and wireless product sales, were $388 million, an increase of nearly 39 percent compared to the restated year-ago quarter.

The robust growth was driven by gains in revenues from value-added business services, consulting services and outsourcing solutions offers and on-line services, including AT&T WorldNet Services. Six months after its introduction, AT&T WorldNet has become the second largest Internet service provider with 425,000 subscribers.

Operating income for communications services declined to $2.209 billion, a 6 percent decrease from the year-ago quarter. Operating margin declined to 17.2 percent from 19.0 percent in the same quarter last year.

Financial services revenue decreased slightly more than 32 percent to $396 million, primarily as a result of the securitization program instituted at AT&T Universal Card Services last year to diversify funding sources as well as increased competition in the consumer credit card business. To date, $6.5 billion of Universal Card Services receivables have been securitized. UCS has undertaken a number of risk management initiatives to improve credit performance due to the increased losses experienced in its portfolio.

UCS expenses for its reward programs also were higher than the third quarter of last year. Financial services had an operating loss for the quarter of $35 million, as compared to an operating profit of $47 million in the year-ago quarter.
The unit's total managed receivables, including those securitized, total $13.0 billion. The number of customer accounts was 18.1 million at the end of the quarter.

Total operating expenses from continuing operations increased $530 million or 5.0 percent for the quarter. Significant increases in selling, general and administrative expenses were partially offset by a decrease in access and other interconnection expenses. The higher SG&A expenses, primarily due to higher marketing and sales expenses in the consumer and wireless businesses as well as growth for initiatives in on-line services, customer care enhancements and preparations to enter the local services business, led to a decrease in operating income of $222 million and a decline in operating margin to 16.4 percent.

Income from discontinued operations increased to $73 million this quarter compared with a significant loss in the year ago quarter primarily due to the third quarter 1995 NCR charge. The income from discontinued operations includes the net income or loss from Lucent Technologies, NCR Corp. and AT&T Capital Corp., as well as Submarine Systems and New Media. Discontinued operations results also include certain adjustments to report AT&T on a consolidated basis, such as the elimination of inter-company sales, taxes on a consolidated basis and an allocation of interest expense based on the net assets of discontinued operations.

AT&T intends to spin off NCR to shareowners by the end of 1996. However, the company said that it will continue for the near term to report NCR's results as it always has. Lucent Technologies will issue its third-quarter financial results separately next week and AT&T Capital reported results earlier this week.

Demonstrating continued progress in its restructuring plan, NCR reported operating income of $29 million, an improvement from the $196 million operating loss excluding restructuring and other charges in the year-ago period.

NCR reported that total revenue, which includes sales to AT&T, Lucent and AT&T Capital Corp., declined more than 18 percent to $1.658 billion for the quarter, reflecting the decision to no longer sell personal computers through volume retail channels. When the effects of this decision are taken into account for both periods, revenues in the quarter were basically flat.

NCR's gross margin increased from the prior year quarter by $85 million. Gross margin as a percentage of revenue improved by 9.6 percentage points. Excluding the restructuring and other charges, expenses decreased nearly 24 percent, or $140 million, from the year ago quarter, and declined 1.9 points as a percent of revenue. -0-
